strategy.mode: metadata-first, deterministic, OpenAIRE-aligned export plus richer internal JSON
strategy.title_policy: Single export title only. Multilingual or alternative titles are preserved in internal.title_variants.
strategy.language_policy: dc:language is treated as the resource language. Multilingual metadata literal languages are tracked separately in internal.metadata_languages.
strategy.dates_policy: Export dates are limited to Accepted, Available, Issued. Available falls back to Issued when absent. Submitted, Created and Modified stay in internal.internal_dates.
strategy.alternate_identifier_policy: Internal article IDs are not exported as OpenAIRE alternateIdentifiers; they are preserved only in internal.article_ID/object_ID.
strategy.description_policy: Preserve multilingual DC.Description entries when present.
strategy.files_policy: citation_pdf_url is preferred for oaire:file/fulltext extraction; viewer URLs are deterministically converted to download URLs for internal PDF assets and local PDF saving.
strategy.references_policy: All citation_reference values are preserved as supplemental data; no promotion to OpenAIRE relatedIdentifier.
strategy.warning_diagnostics_policy: If enabled, warnings can trigger an advisory OpenAI call with automatic second attempt and user-controlled further retry loop; AI output is supplemental and never mutates extracted metadata automatically.

descriptions.value: Building on some international research that emphasises the importance of presenting male models of readers to encourage boys to read, this paper is an exploratory study of reader models in painting and literature. Through a web search among sites linking reading and painting, some 250 paintings depicting men and women reading were analysed. The aim was to observe the frequency of female and male presences but above all to analyse the ways in which they are portrayed and any differences. Finally, we chose some famous texts from children's literature containing characters who read and we also examined the ways in which female and male readers are portrayed. Within the limits of the sample, the results show that there is a tendency to represent more women or girls readers. Furthermore, in the representation, the characteristics attributed to male and female reading change: female reading is mainly related to the theme of pleasure and the search for one's own identity, whereas male reading is more related to study and information. In future studies, it would be interesting to understand whether these different representations influence boys' and girls' relationship with reading.

Basandosi su alcune ricerche internazionali che sottolineano l’importanza di presentare modelli maschili di lettori per incoraggiare i ragazzi a leggere, il contributo presenta uno studio esplorativo sui modelli di lettori nella pittura e nella letteratura. Attraverso una ricerca web tra siti che collegano lettura e pittura, sono stati analizzati circa 250 dipinti raffiguranti uomini e donne intenti alla lettura. L’obiettivo era osservare la frequenza delle presenze femminili e maschili, analizzare i modi in cui sono ritratti ed eventuali differenze. Infine, sono stati selezionati alcuni famosi testi della letteratura per ragazzi che contengono personaggi che leggono e sono stati esaminati i modi in cui lettrici e lettori sono rappresentati. Nei limiti del campione, i risultati mostrano una tendenza a rappresentare più lettrici donne o ragazze. Inoltre, nella rappresentazione, le caratteristiche attribuite alla lettura maschile e femminile cambiano: la lettura femminile è principalmente legata al tema del piacere e alla ricerca della propria identità, mentre la lettura maschile è più associata allo studio e all’acquisizione di informazioni. In studi futuri, sarebbe interessante capire se queste diverse rappresentazioni influenzano la relazione dei ragazzi e delle ragazze con la lettura.

def _extract_openaire_and_internal_dates(self, file_bundle: Dict[str, Any], interactive_resolution: bool = False, ai_config: Optional[Dict[str, Any]] = None) -> Dict[str, Any]:
        citation_date = iso_date(self.meta.first("citation_date"))
        dc_created = iso_date(self.meta.first("DC.Date.created"))
        dc_submitted = iso_date(self.meta.first("DC.Date.dateSubmitted"))
        dc_issued = iso_date(self.meta.first("DC.Date.issued"))
        dc_modified = iso_date(self.meta.first("DC.Date.modified"))
        dc_accepted = iso_date(self.meta.first("DC.Date.accepted"))
        dc_available = iso_date(self.meta.first("DC.Date.available"))
        dom_submitted = iso_date(self._dd_value_after_dt("Inviata"))
        dom_published = iso_date(self._dd_value_after_dt("Pubblicato"))
        pdf_dates = self._extract_pdf_editorial_dates(file_bundle)
        page_rights = self._extract_page_rights_holder_and_year()

        def choose_published_date(citation_date, dom_published, dc_created, dc_issued, dc_modified):
            return citation_date or dom_published or dc_created or dc_issued or dc_modified

        page_candidates = {
            "title": self.meta.first("citation_title") or self.meta.first("DC.Title") or self._text("h1.article-page__title span"),
            "submitted_date": dc_submitted or dom_submitted,
            "accepted_date": dc_accepted,
            "copyright_holder": page_rights.get("copyright_holder_page"),
            "copyright_year": str(page_rights.get("copyright_year_page")) if page_rights.get("copyright_year_page") is not None else None,
            "license_url": self._extract_access_rights_and_license().get("licenseCondition", {}).get("uri"),
        }
        pdf_ai_diag = self._request_ai_pdf_front_analysis(pdf_dates, page_candidates, ai_config)
        pdf_ai_result = pdf_ai_diag.get("result") if isinstance(pdf_ai_diag, dict) and pdf_ai_diag.get("status") == "ok" else {}
        pdf_fields = pdf_ai_result.get("pdf_fields", {}) if isinstance(pdf_ai_result, dict) else {}
        ai_resolution = pdf_ai_result.get("resolution", {}) if isinstance(pdf_ai_result, dict) else {}

        pdf_submitted_value = normalize_space((pdf_fields.get("submitted_date") or {}).get("value")) or pdf_dates.get("submitted_pdf")
        pdf_accepted_value = normalize_space((pdf_fields.get("accepted_date") or {}).get("value")) or pdf_dates.get("accepted_pdf")
        pdf_copyright_holder = normalize_space((pdf_fields.get("copyright_holder") or {}).get("value")) or pdf_dates.get("copyright_holder_pdf")
        pdf_copyright_year = normalize_space((pdf_fields.get("copyright_year") or {}).get("value")) or (str(pdf_dates.get("copyright_year_pdf")) if pdf_dates.get("copyright_year_pdf") is not None else None)
        pdf_title_value = normalize_space((pdf_fields.get("title") or {}).get("value"))
        pdf_title_allowed = bool((pdf_fields.get("title") or {}).get("use_allowed")) if isinstance(pdf_fields.get("title"), dict) else False

        strong_page_published = citation_date or dom_published or dc_created
        if strong_page_published and dc_issued and strong_page_published != dc_issued:
            self._warn(
                code="PUBLISHED_DATE_CONFLICT",
                message=f"Published-date conflict: stronger page signal '{strong_page_published}' overrides DC.Date.issued '{dc_issued}'.",
                function_name="_extract_openaire_and_internal_dates",
                context={
                    "citation_date": citation_date,
                    "dom_published": dom_published,
                    "dc_created": dc_created,
                    "dc_issued": dc_issued,
                    "dc_modified": dc_modified,
                },
            )

        issued = choose_published_date(
            citation_date,
            dom_published,
            dc_created,
            dc_issued,
            dc_modified,
        )
        available = dc_available or issued
        submitted_resolution = self._resolve_discrepancy("submitted_date", dc_submitted or dom_submitted, pdf_submitted_value, interactive_resolution, prefer="pdf", ai_resolution=ai_resolution.get("submitted_date") if isinstance(ai_resolution, dict) else None)
        accepted_resolution = self._resolve_discrepancy("accepted_date", dc_accepted, pdf_accepted_value, interactive_resolution, prefer="pdf", ai_resolution=ai_resolution.get("accepted_date") if isinstance(ai_resolution, dict) else None)
        copyright_holder_resolution = self._resolve_discrepancy("copyright_holder", page_rights.get("copyright_holder_page"), pdf_copyright_holder, interactive_resolution, prefer="pdf", ai_resolution=ai_resolution.get("copyright_holder") if isinstance(ai_resolution, dict) else None)
        copyright_year_resolution = self._resolve_discrepancy(
            "copyright_year",
            str(page_rights.get("copyright_year_page")) if page_rights.get("copyright_year_page") is not None else None,
            pdf_copyright_year,
            interactive_resolution,
            prefer="pdf",
            ai_resolution=ai_resolution.get("copyright_year") if isinstance(ai_resolution, dict) else None,
        )
        title_resolution = self._resolve_discrepancy(
            "title",
            page_candidates.get("title"),
            pdf_title_value if pdf_title_allowed or not page_candidates.get("title") else None,
            interactive_resolution,
            prefer="page",
            ai_resolution=ai_resolution.get("title") if isinstance(ai_resolution, dict) else None,
        )

        accepted = accepted_resolution.get("chosen_value")
        submitted = submitted_resolution.get("chosen_value")

        export_dates: List[Dict[str, Any]] = []
        if accepted:
            export_dates.append({"value": accepted, "dateType": "Accepted", "source": accepted_resolution.get("chosen_source")})
        if available:
            export_dates.append({"value": available, "dateType": "Available", "source": "meta:DC.Date.available" if dc_available else "fallback:Issued"})
        if issued:
            export_dates.append({"value": issued, "dateType": "Issued", "source": "meta:DC.Date.issued" if dc_issued else "meta:citation_date" if citation_date else "dom:Pubblicato" if dom_published else "meta:DC.Date.created"})

        export_dates = dedupe_list(export_dates)
        dates_by_type: Dict[str, Optional[str]] = {d["dateType"]: d["value"] for d in export_dates}
        if not dates_by_type.get("Available") and issued:
            dates_by_type["Available"] = issued
        internal_dates = {
            "submitted": submitted,
            "accepted": accepted,
            "created": dc_created,
            "modified": dc_modified,
            "issued": issued,
            "available": dates_by_type.get("Available"),
            "submitted_page": dc_submitted or dom_submitted,
            "submitted_pdf": pdf_dates.get("submitted_pdf"),
            "accepted_page": dc_accepted,
            "accepted_pdf": pdf_dates.get("accepted_pdf"),
        }
        resolutions = {
            "title": title_resolution,
            "submitted": submitted_resolution,
            "accepted": accepted_resolution,
            "copyright_holder": copyright_holder_resolution,
            "copyright_year": copyright_year_resolution,
        }
        return {
            "export_dates": export_dates,
            "dates_by_type": dates_by_type,
            "internal_dates": internal_dates,
            "pdf_editorial_dates": pdf_dates,
            "page_rights": page_rights,
            "resolutions": resolutions,
            "pdf_ai_resolution": pdf_ai_diag,
        }

pdf_first_page.body_text_excerpt: Parere analogo è fornito dal gruppo di lavoro “ EU high level group of experts on literacy ” istituito nel 2011 dalla Commissione Europea per riflettere e stabilire linee di azione a fronte dei risultati PISA 2009; nel rapporto conclusivo, parlando delle strategie per aumentare la lettura dei ragazzi, si afferma l’importanza dei modelli di genere e degli stereotipi connessi quali fattori che influenzano l’approccio maschile alla let- tura: “Ensuring visibility of male role models showing reading as a masculine activity is crucial. ” (EU high level group of experts on literacy, 2012, p. 49). Il quadro attuale italiano ed europeo sembra dunque presentare un universo maschile poco interessato ai libri, nel quale è possibile ipotizzare un modello culturale che si tramanda implicitamente di padre in figlio: i padri che non leggono difficilmente incoraggiano i figli a farlo e soprattutto non promuovono l’immagine del lettore nelle nuove generazioni creando così uno stereotipo che si consolida nel tempo (Clark, 2009). A partire da queste riflessioni sul modello, si è scelto di modificare lo sguardo d’indagine per esplorare i modelli offerti dall’immaginario figurativo e letterario occidentale. L ’intento non è di cercare nessi di causalità ma di conoscere, in prima istanza, quali rappresentazioni siano state prodotte sul soggetto che legge e riflettere sulle implicazioni di genere. 2.
